about: The blocks Claude writes in a reply for the app to draw with buttons: one catalog for the guidance Claude gets (bin/amarchy REPLY_FORMAT), the app that draws them (chat.js replyParts, artifactParts) and the check when a turn ends (bin/amarchy reply_issues). A block is a fenced block named for its kind, its attributes key="value" on the opening line, its body under it. Attribute types: text, phone, email, datetime (ISO 8601 with a time and an offset), url, path, session (a chat's id), one of a list (enum). Body shapes: text, code, url (its first line), todos (- [ ] lines), options (- Label | message), fields (Label: value lines; a block with labels takes only those), series (Label: number lines, or a markdown table: labels, then a column of numbers per series).

example.body: the whole message, ready to send

blocks.for: a command for them to run
a link for them to open

example.attrs: label="Sign in to Gmail" note="Expires in 10 minutes"
title="ECOS panel" when="2026-10-29T15:40:00-05:00" end="2026-10-29T17:00:00-05:00" where="Teatro Panorama, Bogotá"

example.body:
- [ ] Send the C21 summary (today)
- [x] Twilio top-up

blocks.rule: Lists they track (still open, waiting on, loops) go in a todos block, every time you list them.

blocks.for: the details of one thing, label by label (an invoice, an account, a booking)
numbers worth seeing as a chart (a trend, a comparison)
blocks.rule: A chart takes "Label: number" lines (one series), or a markdown table for several: the labels, then a column of numbers per series. bar compares, line shows a trend over time. Only real numbers you have, at most 8 series.

example.attrs: name="Spinning Center Rosales" where="Cl. 72 #5-83, Bogotá" hours="Mon-Fri 6am-9pm"

blocks.for: another chat (one you started, or one this is about)
a file you made for them
the briefing a reply of more than a few lines ends with

example.body:
Done: what you did or found, in one line (Answer: instead, when they asked a question)
Checked: how you verified it (leave the row out when there was nothing to verify)
Open: what's left, or what you're unsure of (leave it out when nothing)
Next: the next step you'd take (leave it out when none)
You: what they need to do now, or Nothing

blocks.rule: The brief block is the reply in a few rows, for someone who reads nothing else: only those labels, in that order, one short line each (no lists, no detail: that's what the sections are for). It comes after the last section, before your choices and the goal.

blocks.for: a question for them, answered with a tap

example.body:
- Ship it | Ship it: merge to main and push
- Not yet

blocks.rule: Any question you ask them, a yes or no included, goes in a choices block at the end, so they answer with a tap; each option (at most 4) is "- Label | the full message it sends" (or just "- Label").

blocks.for: this chat's goal and where it stands

example.body: Make Today the app's home screen

blocks.rule: The very end of every reply is this chat's goal and where it stands, in a goal block (it isn't shown in the reply: the app puts the goal under the chat's name and on its Today page, and offers to close a done chat). state is working (more to do, or under way), waiting (you need them: your choices block says what), blocked (you can't go on), or done (the goal is reached: built and shipped, answered, sent; nothing is left for this chat). When it's done, give them a link block to see or check the result (the page, the deploy, the PR, the document) whenever there is one. The goal is one short sentence of what they want from this chat, the same every reply unless it changed:
